item.title: Arash Markazi on CNN: The NFL wants to own every holiday
item.description: The Sporting Tribune founder and CEO Arash Markazi joined CNN on Thursday, fresh off covering the Rams' 26-13 win over the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium, to talk about the NFL's growing grip on the holiday calendar. The league has played on Thanksgiving for decades and now has games scheduled on Thanksgiving Eve, Black Friday, Christmas and New Year's Eve, with the Super Bowl falling on Valentine's Day this season. Markazi said the strategy is simple. "Football is king in this country," Markazi said, noting that NFL games make up the vast majority of the most-watched broadcasts in the country each year. He said the league targets days when families are together and nobody is working, so it can reach casual viewers as well as die-hard fans. "Where can we get the periphery fans?" Markazi said. "Where can we get the people who don't normally watch?" Markazi was at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday night for the NFL's Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix, which included a U2 performance, and said the event delivered. "It felt like a mini Super Bowl," he said. "If there were any concerns about how Thanksgiving Eve would do, that was laid to rest. It will be here for a long time." Markazi traced the shift back to Christmas Day, which used to belong to the NBA. "Christmas Day was basketball," he said. "They said, 'No, no, no. Christmas Day is our day too.'" He also broke down Amazon's Black Friday game, which is being made available beyond Prime members this year as the company leans into shopping during the broadcast. "Most people are home on Black Friday, they're shopping," Markazi said. "And now a sports fan can be watching the football game and shopping at the same time." The conversation ended with Aaron Rodgers, whose public split with the Pittsburgh Steelers after being benched and released has become one of the stories of the season. "This is better than anything on Bravo," Markazi said. "This is better than 'Real Housewives.'" Markazi called Rodgers a first-ballot Hall of Famer and "maybe a top-five quarterback of all time," but said the drama likely marks the end of his career. "No one needs this kind of baggage," he said. "But you want to talk about going out in a blaze of glory."

item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images After beating the Utah Jazz 109-94 on Monday , the Los Angeles Lakers are now 15-3 and one game ahead of the San Antonio Spurs for the best record in the NBA. They’ve won 11 of their last 12 games, are 8-2 at home and 7-1 on the road, and have done all of that with Austin Reaves missing their last five games . Luka Doncic is playing at maybe his craziest MVP level yet , averaging 36.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, 7.7 assists, and 1.8 steals per game, while Reaves is putting up 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 4.7 assists on 51.3% shooting from the field and 40.9% from three. But here’s where things get interesting for Lakers fans. Some of the best teams in franchise history had a similar 15-win start to their seasons, going all the way back to the Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O’Neal days, and even the first year of LeBron James and Anthony Davis playing together. So, let’s go back and see what happened to those teams, how their playoff runs went, and what we can take from them when looking at the Lakers this season. 2001-02 Lakers: NBA Champions Start: 16-2 Final Record: 58-24 (3rd in the West) Coming off back-to-back championships, the Lakers opened the 2001-02 season with 16 wins in their first 18 games under Phil Jackson. And when you had two of the five best players in the NBA on the same team, there wasn’t much anybody could do against them. Shaq averaged 27.2 points, 10.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 2.0 blocks on 57.9% shooting from the field that season, while Kobe was already putting up 25.2 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 5.5 assists at just 23 years old. They also had Robert Horry, Derek Fisher, and Rick Fox playing their roles around the two stars. The Lakers finished with 58 wins and entered the playoffs as the third seed, behind the Sacramento Kings and the Spurs . They swept the Portland Trail Blazers in the first round and beat the Spurs in five games before facing the Kings in one of the most memorable Western Conference Finals ever. The Kings had a 3-2 series lead, and the Lakers needed to win Game 6 at home and Game 7 on the road to keep their championship hopes alive. They did exactly that, winning Game 7 in overtime behind 35 points and 13 rebounds from Shaq. The NBA Finals against the New Jersey Nets weren’t nearly as competitive. The Lakers swept them in four games, with O’Neal averaging 36.3 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 2.8 blocks to win his third straight Finals MVP. item.title: Germany's Freigang banned over drugs test issues
item.description: Laura Freigang has scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany [Getty Images] Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests. The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027. The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June. The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement. The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026. Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October. All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected. This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga. Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan. In a club statement , Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship". Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027. Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura. "The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition. "The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player." item.description: The marching band for the University of Southern California Trojans football team has been ousted from an upcoming Rose Bowl game with its rival team, the UCLA Bruins, over a prank involving a lewd phrase. However, despite that imbalance, Roma was seldom, if ever, reticent on Wednesday evening, facing PSG with the same pluck and gusto that had allowed Gasperini’s side to build early leads against Real Madrid and Manchester United. item.title: Skip Bayless’ scathing Mike McCarthy nickname resurfaces after Aaron Rodgers sleeping claims
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images Skip Bayless’ old criticism of Mike McCarthy has resurfaced after Aaron Rodgers accused the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach of falling asleep during team meetings. The NFL pundit gave McCarthy the nickname ‘Mike McSleepy’ back in 2021, and his comments have taken on a new relevance following Rodgers’ recent allegations. Rodgers claimed McCarthy arrived late to a quarterbacks’ meeting, fell asleep twice while snoring loudly and then walked out without explanation. The former Green Bay Packers quarterback suggested this was not an isolated incident, as similar behaviour had taken place during their previous years together. However, this is not the first time McCarthy has faced questions about his alertness during games and meetings. Bayless famously took aim at the coach on Fox Sports’ Undisputed after the Dallas Cowboys suffered a 23-19 defeat to the New York Giants in January 2021. The Cowboys entered that game at 6-9 and needed a victory to keep their playoff hopes alive. Instead, they lost to the Giants and missed the postseason, prompting Bayless to deliver a lengthy rant about McCarthy’s role on the sideline. “What have I had a problem with all year long? I’ve sat over here and said this 100 times this season. I keep asking: What does Mike McCarthy do on the sideline? He doesn’t call plays; he doesn’t overrule or rule on special teams; he just sort of stands over there with his hands in his pockets, blinking and looking around like, ‘Am I the head coach?’ I’m not sure. “Mike McCarthy is Mike McSleepy. He has challenged two plays the whole year and I’m saying, ‘Who is he and what is he doing over there?’ You know what a pond looks like with a frog on a lilypad; he’s like a big old bullfrog on a lilypad just sunning himself on Sunday afternoon.” Bayless’ comments have resurfaced amid the growing controversy surrounding McCarthy’s treatment of Rodgers and the 42-year-old’s departure from Pittsburgh. item.title: Jordie Barrett to captain All Blacks for first time in England rematch
item.description: Jordie Barrett will follow in the footsteps of elder brothers Scott and Beauden as he captains New Zealand for the first time in their rematch with England . Hooker Codie Taylor, who had been deputising for regular skipper Ardie Savea, has been ruled out of the encounter with a tight calf, with the youngest Barrett brother installed as Dave Rennie seeks a response following a record defeat last week. The All Blacks were beaten 37-12 by England, and are bidding to avoid becoming the first New Zealand side to be beaten by their opposition in three successive contests. Richie Mo’unga takes over at fly half from Damian McKenzie, who shifts to full-back with Beauden Barrett displaced from the starting side. Leicester Fainga’anuku partners the captain in midfield with Anton Lienert-Brown another injury absentee, while Anton Segner is the replacement for Tupou Vaa’i on the blindside flank. Cam Roigard also drops to the bench with Cortez Ratima preferred as Mo’unga’s half-back partner. “That was a pretty simple choice for us,” head coach Rennie said of the appointment of captain. “I think anyone who has worked with Jordie would know he is very impressive, has a great game understanding on both sides of the ball. He’s prepared to challenge. “He’s been great in our leadership group and he’s taken over the captaincy role when Codie has left the field. It was a pretty straightforward decision for us.” New Zealand XV: 1 Ethan de Groot, 2 Asafo Aumua, 3 Fletcher Newell; 4 Scott Barrett , 5 Fabian Holland; 6 Anton Segner, 7 Peter Lakai, 8 Wallace Sititi; 9 Cortez Ratima, 10 Richie Mo’unga; 11 Josh Moorby, 12 Jordie Barrett (capt.), 13 Leicester Fainga’anuku, 14 Rieko Ioane; 15 Damian McKenzie. item.title: JJ Redick Reveals When He Was Convinced Lakers Had To Sign Ziaire Williams
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers brought in many new faces this past offseason, and Ziaire Williams has proven to be one of their better acquisitions. There wasn’t much hype about Williams’ arrival, but Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed at Wednesday’s practice that all it took was one meeting to convince him they had to sign the forward. “I’ve been collecting intel on players for 20 years now,” Redick said, via Infanity TV. “I did it as a player, I did it in media, I do it now as a coach, so yeah you certainly want to bring the right people in here… Ziaire was supposed to make six and a half million, I think, from Brooklyn this year, and then he was a non-guaranteed deal, so they waive him. “He becomes a free agent, and he was willing to go to a gym in Vegas and work out for our coaching staff and for Rob [Pelinka],” Redick continued. “We put him through that; he looked great. I met with him the next day at the hotel for about 45 minutes, and towards the middle of that conversation, I just kept thinking to myself, holy s***, we got to get this guy in our locker room. We need this guy to be a Laker.” Williams hit free agency after the Brooklyn Nets didn’t pick up his $6.25 million team option for 2026-27. The Lakers were immediately linked to the 25-year-old , as he had fans inside their facility. Redick then joined that group of fans after meeting Williams for the first time. The 42-year-old felt the Lakers had to get him in, and it doesn’t look like they faced much competition. Why? Well, the Lakers signed Williams to just a one-year, $3 million deal . That’s looking like quite a bargain now. Williams is averaging 9.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.1 blocks per game in 2026-27 while shooting 53.8% from the field and 42.1% from beyond the arc. He has been the kind of athletic 3-and-D wing the Lakers have been crying out for in recent years. Williams also said in the offseason that Lakers fans can expect a lot of energy and hard work from him on the court . He has been true to his word and is becoming a fan favorite. With role players like Williams impressing and superstar guard Luka Doncic on a tear, the Lakers have gotten off to an excellent 15-3 start to the season. Not many expected them to have the best record in the NBA, but it has now been claimed that this is down to an easy schedule. Well, the Lakers will get a chance to make a statement as they take on the 15-4 San Antonio Spurs next at Frost Bank Center on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET.

item.title: Why Lions might franchise tag Brian Branch instead of signing a contract extension

The Detroit Lions are facing off against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving, and defensive back Brian Branch is going to be key to stopping this high-powered Bears offense. For Branch himself, this week is a huge opportunity to further prove himself in a contract year. Set to hit the open market after 2026, alongside tight end Sam LaPorta, the Lions will have a difficult decision to make with Branch this upcoming offseason. ESPN's Bill Barnwell believes that, instead of a contract extension for Branch, he might be in line for the Lions' franchise tag. The reason why is simple: it's more affordable for Detroit to use the tag on Branch to give them more time to figure out a long-term deal. Why Brian Branch might be franchise tagged by Lions "With the safety franchise tag projected to come in at $22.2 million, the Lions might see tagging him as a logical way to continue their relationship while they negotiate a long-term extension," Barnwell writes. With the Lions having plenty of offseason questions to solve, once the 2026 season comes to a close, being able to tag Branch and figure things out over an extended period of time would be much easier than trying to work out an extension. Since Branch has had an up-and-down NFL career so far, seeing what Branch can do to close out the 2026 NFL season could give the Lions reason to sign him to a long-term deal. But even if he doesn't finish strong, the Lions could still elect to tag him to avoid letting him hit free agency, where he'd surely get plenty of competitive offers from other teams looking for upgrades. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
